solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, answers clash); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thankyou note asks for money

parts.note: TA is informal British for thank you
PS, a postscript, is a note added to a letter

explanation.surface: A thank-you note that ends up asking for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' tempts a musical letter, but here it is the postscript at the foot of a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap someone is informal for begging or borrowing money from them.

clue.text: Set off in time and fixed with engineers inside

indicators.note: the engineers go within the fixed word

parts.note: rigged means fixed dishonestly, as in a rigged vote
RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army

explanation.surface: A bomb set off on schedule after engineers rigged it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link; RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps that turns up often in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off or cause it to start.

clue.text: Pregnant rep lies about investor

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A salesman tells porkies about a backer who is expecting.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeping partner puts money into a business without taking an active role.

clue.text: Learner wearing joke jumper is a clumsy fool

indicators.note: the joke word has the learner inside it, as if wearing it like a garment

parts.note: COD as an adjective or noun means a hoax or joke
L is the learner plate abbreviation
a hopper is anything that jumps

explanation.surface: A trainee in a novelty sweater makes a fool of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater, which 'wearing' supports, but it is something that hops.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a heavy-footed, awkward person, a lumbering oaf.

clue.text: South America invested in oil campaign

indicators.note: the continent's letters are placed within the oil word, as money is put into a venture

parts.note: crude is unrefined oil

explanation.surface: A continent puts money into the oil business as a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade is a vigorous campaign for a cause.

clue.text: Old fools, trapping English wild cats

indicators.note: the fools word catches the English letter inside it

parts.note: clots are British slang for idiots

explanation.surface: Elderly idiots catch an English beast in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocelots are spotted wild cats of Central and South America.

clue.text: Unfortunate — splashed endlessly around

indicators.note: the remaining letters are moved around into a new order
the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Poor soul, splashed around and around for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the D off SPLASHED, and 'around' rearranges SPLASHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hapless means unlucky, ill-starred.

clue.text: How Marxists might celebrate a victory?

definitions.text: How Marxists might celebrate a victory?

parts.words: How Marxists might celebrate a victory?
parts.note: read literally, communists, whose colour is red, would colour the whole place their own shade; idiomatically it means a wild night out

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go out and celebrate riotously, with red the colour of communism.

clue.text: Called with electronic compass

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: Phoned about an electronic compass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compass' suggests the navigation device; it means scope or extent.
explanation.definitionFit: Range and compass both mean the full extent or scope of something.

clue.text: Vulnerable European Community protected by guarantee

indicators.note: the Community letters sit inside the guarantee word, sheltered by it

parts.note: to insure is to guarantee against loss

explanation.surface: Europe's trading bloc looks exposed despite having a guarantee.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insecure is unprotected and so open to attack or harm.

clue.text: Voting system is working in gaol

parts.note: PR stands for proportional representation
taken as written
on means operating, switched on

explanation.surface: The electoral method is up and running in a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link before the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaol is the British spelling of jail, a synonym for a place of imprisonment.

clue.text: King George and father grab a quiet drink

indicators.note: the king and father letters seize the next pair and hold them in their middle

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is King George's royal cipher
PA is an informal word for father
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A monarch and his dad sneak off for a discreet tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy distilled from grape residue, a strong spirit.

clue.text: In the long run such work may be offered

definitions.meaning: split as two words it means gradually, as time passes
extra hours beyond the normal working day that an employer may offer

explanation.definitionFit: Over time means eventually, and overtime is additional paid work beyond normal hours.

clue.text: Ruin most of planet

indicators.note: the planet word drops its last letter

parts.note: Mars is a planet

explanation.surface: Wrecking most of a world.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to spoil or damage.

clue.text: Bed rest taken regularly after some golf game

indicators.note: the regular letters come after the golf word in the answer

parts.note: a round is a session of golf

indicators.note: every second letter of the two words is picked out in turn

explanation.surface: After a round of golf, a lie-in is in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounders is a British bat-and-ball game, a children's sport similar to baseball.

clue.text: Field sports, initially with copper present

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word sports is used

parts.note: P stands for penny, a copper coin in Britain
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A sports ground where a policeman happens to be on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman or the metal Cu; it is the coin, abbreviated P.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a field of activity or area of influence, as in a sphere of expertise.

clue.text: Always popular, the first lady runs without experience

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
green means inexperienced, a novice

explanation.surface: A pioneering woman runs without any track record.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evergreen stays fresh and popular for ever, like a classic song.

clue.text: Copies given to doctor — that's curtains!

indicators.note: the copies are handed over to the doctor, so they follow the doctor's letters

parts.note: to ape is to imitate, so apes means copies

explanation.surface: Handing your imitations to the doctor spells the end for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's curtains!' sounds like doom but simply means window hangings.
explanation.definitionFit: Drapes is a chiefly American word for long heavy curtains.

clue.text: Mourn the French way?

definitions.meaning: to regret or grieve over something
the French word for a street, which is a way

explanation.definitionFit: Rue is to regret bitterly, and in French rue means street.

clue.text: Block sources of support and help useless posh bloke

indicators.note: the starts of the three words supply the opening letters

parts.note: a toff is British slang for an upper-class man

explanation.surface: Cut off support and assistance for a worthless upper-class chap.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut off is to stop a flow or close something down.

clue.text: A lot live dangerously, liable to explode

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are thrown about with reckless abandon

explanation.surface: Plenty of people live risky lives near something explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: A volatile substance is unstable and may readily explode or evaporate.

clue.text: One who calls for victory — is it over outside?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the outer letters of the word over are used

explanation.surface: A supporter shouts for a win, asking if the match is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; 'outside' takes the first and last letters of 'over', O and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor is someone who calls round at your house.

clue.text: Nothing found in unusually labile plant

indicators.note: the nothing letter is located within the jumbled letters
the letters are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is stable in an unpredictable plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges LABILE into LBELIA, and 'found in' places O after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a flowering plant popular for bedding and hanging baskets.

clue.text: Put up with topless yobbos and aggressive moves

parts.note: to bear something is to tolerate it

indicators.note: the roughnecks word loses its top letter

parts.note: yobbos are British slang for loutish hooligans, roughly thugs

explanation.surface: Tolerating shirtless louts and their threatening behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' suggests bare-chested yobs but means the first letter of the synonym goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bear hugs are crushing embraces, used in wrestling as aggressive holds.

clue.text: Live group getting besieged

parts.note: to be means to live or exist
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A live band getting mobbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Beset means surrounded or harassed on all sides, besieged.

clue.text: Showing respect after victory in quagmire

indicators.note: the victory word goes inside the swamp word

parts.note: a bog is a soft wet quagmire
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: Bowing to the winner after triumphing in a muddy contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowing, bending the head or body, is a gesture of deference and respect.

clue.text: Religion like this welcoming suggestion

indicators.note: the word for like this takes the suggestion inside it, as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: so means in this way, like this
a hint is a suggestion

explanation.surface: A faith presented in this way is open to suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the indigenous religion of Japan, centred on worship of kami spirits.

clue.text: Grudgingly accept new role in gallery

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go within the gallery name

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery

indicators.note: the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Putting up with a fresh job at an art museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a London art gallery; 'grudgingly' belongs to the definition, not to any mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate is to put up with something one would rather not, enduring it reluctantly.

clue.text: Land and fit rear arm anew

indicators.note: the letters are fitted together again in a different way

explanation.surface: Back on the ground, a soldier has his back arm refitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra firma is Latin for solid ground, dry land as opposed to sea or air.

clue.text: Almost cherished name for man of the church

indicators.note: the cherished word stops one letter short of completion

parts.note: dear means cherished, much loved

explanation.surface: A beloved name for a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is a senior clergyman heading a cathedral chapter.
